profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting is held between the university-based development team and the city MCDRRMO operations office for Project YOLO, a disaster response coordination prototype. The immediate context is Sprint 5: the team plans to deploy a near-final build that includes a crowdsourced incident dashboard, photo-based situation updates, and a shared contact directory for supporting agencies before next Friday's pilot. The agenda is to align on what will be deployed, what operational data MCDRRMO will provide, how photos and reports will flow into the dashboard, and what handoffs each side owns during the pilot week. The expected outcome is a shared-looking agreement on deployment timing, directory content, photo verification flow, and pilot preparation responsibilities.

members.name: Angela Cruz
members.expertise: Agile software delivery, GIS-enabled web/mobile systems, prototype integration
members.background: Angela is the senior student lead coordinating the university research-development team building Project YOLO; she manages sprint planning, interfaces across the web dashboard and mobile reporting app, and demo preparation for government stakeholders.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the prototype scope stable long enough to deliver a polished sprint demo, avoid operational commitments the student team cannot support 24/7, and secure positive feedback from MCDRRMO without reopening core workflow design.
hidden_assumptions: When operations asks for the incident feed, they mean the curated dashboard stream after duplicate reports and obvious noise have already been filtered.
A pilot is successful if a supervised exercise or guided walkthrough can run end-to-end with representative users and realistic sample data.
The agency directory for this sprint only needs formal focal persons from core response agencies already identified during requirements gathering.
Verified photos can be treated as operationally usable once the system checks metadata consistency and a coordinator flags them inside the queue.
If MCDRRMO does not explicitly raise a deployment support issue, they understand the student team is delivering a prototype environment rather than a live operational service.

members.name: Ramon Villanueva
members.expertise: Emergency operations coordination, incident reporting workflows, inter-agency response communication
members.background: Ramon is the duty operations officer assigned to work with the researchers and translate MCDRRMO field coordination needs into system requirements; he regularly coordinates with barangays, rescue units, hospitals, and supporting agencies during response activations.
members.private_state: He wants the tool to fit real command-center use during the rainy season, reduce confusion during actual callouts, and avoid a pilot that looks good in a demo but fails under live information flow.
hidden_assumptions: An incident feed means the live stream of incoming field reports that duty staff use to see everything first before deciding what matters.
A pilot is only meaningful if the system can be used during an actual operational window or at least under live incoming reports from real responders.
The agency directory naturally includes all practical response contacts needed during activation, including barangay focal persons and hospital desks, not just formal agency heads.
A photo counts as verified only after a human at the MCDRRMO duty desk has reviewed it before it is shown broadly to responders.
Because YOLO is meant for coordination, any build described as available next week is assumed to be usable in the normal command-center workflow without researcher hand-holding.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to the system's 'incident feed' as if it were a single obvious artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the deduplicated, moderated stream displayed on the dashboard after system-side filtering and triage rules.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the raw live intake of reports arriving from field users and partner agencies before filtering.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, 'incident feed' sounds like shared operational jargon, so both assume the other is using the standard meaning from their own workflow and neither expects the distinction to matter at this handoff level.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as ready for pilot
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they want the system 'ready for pilot next Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means ready for a guided pilot session or tabletop exercise where the team can walk users through key flows using controlled or sample submissions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means ready to be used in a real operational setting if weather or incident conditions trigger actual reporting next week.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'pilot' is broad and routinely used for both demonstrations and limited real-world use, so surface agreement feels sufficient unless someone explicitly probes the operating conditions.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about finalizing the 'agency directory' for coordination.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the directory includes only core agencies and designated focal persons already documented in the project's formal stakeholder list.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the directory also covers barangay contacts, hospital desks, and other practical response endpoints staff call during live coordination.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: A directory sounds like a supporting artifact rather than a headline design decision, so each person treats their own boundary as obvious and does not enumerate the included contact groups.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say uploaded photos will be 'verified' before broader use.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes verification happens through metadata checks, duplicate detection, and an in-system coordinator flag that marks a photo as acceptable for the dashboard.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes verification requires explicit human review by the MCDRRMO duty officer before responders and partner agencies rely on the image.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the need for verification and neither sees a reason to restate the workflow, because each assumes the method is already implied by normal practice on their side.

turns.inner_thought: I need this sprint frozen enough that we can actually polish the near-final build and not get dragged into last-minute workflow changes. For me, ready for pilot next Friday means we can run a guided session smoothly with the dashboard, sample or controlled submissions, and the main flows behaving end-to-end. If they don't raise deployment support again, I can keep this framed as a prototype environment, not a live service commitment.
turns.utterance: Morning, Ramon. From the dev side, Sprint 5 is in decent shape, and today I'd like us to lock exactly what we need so YOLO is ready for pilot next Friday. We just need to settle the remaining handoffs on data, users, and the dashboard flow.

turns.inner_thought: What operations really needs is something usable in the command center if incoming reports start coming next week. The priority is straightforward: the incident feed has to let duty staff see reports as they arrive, verified photos have to be safe to rely on, and the agency directory has to include the actual people and desks we call during activation. If those are lined up, then the pilot next Friday will mean something operationally.
turns.utterance: Morning, Angela. On our side, the main things we need lined up are the incident feed, verified photos, and the agency directory before next week's pilot window. If those three are stable, the rest should be manageable.

turns.inner_thought: Good, that's consistent with the dashboard features already in the build. The incident feed is already rendering the moderated stream properly, so I don't want to reopen the feed logic. For the agency directory, I just need the latest formal focal-person list from the core agencies so we can create accounts and preload contacts for the demo users.
turns.utterance: That helps. The current build already shows the incident feed on the dashboard, so we're not starting from zero there. If you can send me the latest agency directory sheet today or tomorrow, my team can finalize the accounts and preload the coordination side.

turns.inner_thought: I'll send the updated directory file with the barangay contacts, hospital desks, rescue units, and the rest of the practical chain we use. And yes, the incident feed really matters because the command center needs to see what comes in right away before anything gets decided. I assume that's already what they're building if it's for coordination.
turns.utterance: Yes, I can forward the updated directory sheet. We've added a few more contacts, including some of the units we actually coordinate with most often. And for the incident feed, what matters to us is that the command center can see what comes in immediately, so that will be important during the pilot.

turns.inner_thought: The photo cards are already working after metadata checks and queue flagging, and that's enough for our prototype flow. I should reinforce that the full reporting path is testable now. If users can submit, review, and view those cards in a supervised session, that counts as success for next Friday.
turns.utterance: On the photo side, verified photos are already appearing correctly in the dashboard cards in the latest build. So once we load the updated users, people should be able to practice the full reporting flow during the pilot.

turns.inner_thought: That sounds promising, but verified photos, for us, means the duty desk has already looked at them before anyone out in the response chain treats them as reliable. I don't need to go into detail here because surely that review step is already understood if they're saying 'verified.' I just want to signal that responders may rely on those photos next week.
turns.utterance: That sounds good, as long as verified photos are the ones the duty desk has screened before responders rely on them during next week's pilot use. If that's in place, it should help a lot.

turns.inner_thought: He's aligned on the importance, which is good. For me, once the directory is loaded for the core accounts and a few agency users can submit and view reports end-to-end in the prototype environment, we're ready. I want to define readiness around successful flow completion, not around any open-ended live operations expectation.
turns.utterance: Right. From my side, once the agency directory is loaded and a few agency users can submit and view reports end-to-end, I'll consider the system ready for pilot. At that point we can focus on making the session smooth.

turns.inner_thought: If the weather shifts, we may actually try this in a live window with field units, barangays, and partner desks sending in updates. So the directory really needs the normal contact chain we use, not just the top-level offices. I assume when she says the system is ready for pilot, she means ready enough to slot into actual operations if needed.
turns.utterance: Understood. And just so you know, if weather conditions worsen, we may try using YOLO with field units and partner desks, so having the normal contact chain in the agency directory will be helpful. That way the pilot is closer to how we really coordinate.

turns.inner_thought: I should keep the handoff crisp and avoid committing us to anything like round-the-clock operational support. We'll deploy the updated dashboard and the queue used for photo review, and they can provide the directory file and participant names. As long as we have those inputs by midweek, the guided pilot can run cleanly.
turns.utterance: Okay, let me summarize the handoff so we're aligned. The dev team will deploy the updated dashboard and the verification queue, and MCDRRMO will send the agency directory file plus the pilot participants by midweek. If we keep to that timeline, next Friday should stay on track.

turns.inner_thought: That works for me. If the build is available by then, we'll treat it as something we can use in the normal command-center flow during the pilot window. The incident feed, especially, should reduce confusion once reports start coming in next Friday.
turns.utterance: Agreed. We'll send what you need on our side, and the incident feed should make coordination smoother once the pilot starts next Friday. Let's proceed on that basis.
